prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: underground/surface railway; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour patterns. Communications-Based Train Control system (CBTC) supervises separation/authority/regulation; control room strategy, train/wayside protection.
Line Traffic Controller monitors/authorizes/coordin­ates service/recovery; Revenue Train Operator handles readiness/cab/passenger procedures/instructions. Voice Dispatch Console provides degraded-service coordination, separate from vital data.
Metro Operations Control System (Lantern): positions/regulation/alarms/commands; sends Crew Login Token Bundle. Service Timetable Server supplies non-vital schedule context. Passenger Information Gateway receives non-vital position/service state, distributes approved messages; cannot influence safety.
North District Zone Controller/South District Zone Controller derive safe authority from location/occupancy/field state. East Junction Interlocking/West Junction Interlocking control vital points/signals, accept safety-compliant commands; safety-channel indications reach onboard.
Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): validates authority sequence/applicability/consistency; supervises protection/speed/doors/train commands. Activation requires authentication, energization, valid integrity. States: initialization, protected manual operation, automatic train operation, fallback operation, cutout. Recalculates braking demand each enforcement cycle; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log after enforcement-data validation.
Dual Channel Odometer supplies independent speed/distance; continuous comparison triggers degradation above divergence threshold. Reduced confidence increases uncertainty and separation-preserving action requests. Trainborne propulsion/braking interface converts safety commands, preserving non-vital electrical isolation. Brake assurance monitors feedback/pressure/deceleration for service/emergency availability.
Train Radio Modem maintains sessions over Wayside Radio Access Network; radio reports quality/registration/continuity onboard. Safety Data Communication Network: deterministic/segregated/availability-monitored transport requiring integrity/authentication/bounded latency; sends Clock Drift Sample Report at synchronization intervals.
Operator interface presents authority/speed/confidence/radio/actions; monitored acknowledgements reject stale/inconsistent commands. Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges enable/closed-and-locked indications when correctly berthed.
Maintenance Diagnostic Server (Quarry) collects non-vital trainborne health for Signal Maintenance Engineer (Maple), without vital access/authority bypass. Cyber Security Officer oversees access/security response; Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports communications keys without altering safety logic.
Degraded: rulebook-safe state/reduced automation/human confirmation/conservative movement; confidence/communications loss or vital disagreement restricts movement pending resolution/approved procedure.

New part:
S051: Wayside communications for Greenvale Metro are organized around continuous train radio coverage and a separated safety data backbone that carries vital movement authority traffic.
S052: The Wayside Radio Access Network is sometimes called Saffron in radio survey records, but this document uses Wayside Radio Access Network as the canonical name.
S053: The Wayside Radio Access Network provides overlapping cell coverage through stations, tunnels, crossovers, and depot approach tracks so that the Train Radio Modem can maintain a stable session during normal operation.
S054: Radio sites are engineered with sector overlap at station throats and interlocking approaches because these locations combine frequent braking, switching, and train-to-wayside message activity.
S055: The Train Radio Modem maintains the active bearer used by the Atlas Onboard Controller and reports radio quality changes before the session reaches the minimum design margin.
S056: Handover is planned as a make-before-break event where practical, with the old radio path retained until the new path has accepted the session and passed basic message checks.
S057: If radio quality degrades faster than predicted, the onboard equipment falls back to the last validated movement authority rules rather than accepting unverified wayside data.
S058: The Safety Data Communication Network carries vital messages between zone controllers, interlockings, and approved interfaces using deterministic routing and monitored latency limits.
S059: The Safety Data Communication Network is physically and logically separated from maintenance and passenger information traffic to reduce exposure to congestion and non-vital configuration changes.
S060: Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the authentication framework used on the safety data paths and is managed under controlled access by authorized technical staff.
S061: North District Zone Controller is sometimes called Marble in legacy boundary diagrams, but this document uses North District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
S062: South District Zone Controller is sometimes called Orchid in commissioning notes, but this document uses South District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
S063: North District Zone Controller supervises the northern main line, the northern turnback, and the approach to East Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
S064: South District Zone Controller supervises the southern main line, the southern turnback, and the approach to West Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
S065: The boundary between North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller is defined by track section ownership, radio coverage overlap, and the point at which a train authority must be reissued by the receiving zone.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
